title: Rome Fiumicino airport to the city: train, bus or taxi?
summary: Every way from Fiumicino into Rome, with the official fares: the €14 Leonardo Express, the €8 FL1 train, buses from €4 and the €55 fixed taxi fare.
answer: For most people the Leonardo Express is the easy choice: €14, 32 minutes, non-stop to Roma Termini, every 15 minutes. Three or four people heading for a hotel inside the historic centre often do better in a licensed white taxi at the fixed fare of €55 per car. With time to spare, the buses start at €4.

body:
## The options side by side

| Option | One way | Time | Where it leaves you |
|---|---|---|---|
| Leonardo Express train | €14 | 32 min, non-stop | Roma Termini |
| FL1 regional train | €8 | not published | Other Rome stations, such as Tiburtina and Ostiense |
| SIT Bus Shuttle | €7 online, €2 more at the stop | timetable times are "indicative" | Via Crescenzio (Vatican area), Termini (Via Marsala) |
| Terravision bus | from €4 | about 40 to 50 min, by its own page | Termini |
| Cotral bus | €5, €7 bought on board | not published | Termini and Tiburtina |
| Licensed taxi | €55 per car, fixed | about 40 to 50 min | Your door, inside the Aurelian Walls |
| Pre-booked private transfer | quoted when you book | depends on traffic | Your door |

All fares are the operators' own, read on 12 November 2026. The airport is about 32 km from the city centre, according to Aeroporti di Roma (ADR), which runs it.

## Leonardo Express: the default for most people

Trenitalia's Leonardo Express is the non-stop train between the airport station and **Roma Termini**. Its own page gives the fare as **€14**, the journey as **32 minutes** and departures **every 15 minutes**. ADR lists the first and last trains from the airport as **05:38** and **23:27**, and from Termini as 04:50 and 23:05.

Three rules on the Trenitalia page are worth knowing:

- **Groups of four** pay €40 instead of €56, if all four tickets are bought in one transaction.
- **Children under 4** travel free, and for every paying adult, one child aged 4 to 11 travels free too.
- **Luggage is free**, including large cases. Integrated Metrebus city tickets are **not** valid on this train.

Termini is Rome's main station and the hub of the metro, so from there you can change to metro lines A and B, a bus, or the taxi rank.

## FL1 regional train: cheaper, and better for some neighbourhoods

The FL1 is an ordinary regional line that starts at the airport and runs across the city (Trenitalia's fare sheet names the route Fiumicino – Roma – Fara Sabina – Orte). The fare from the airport to stations inside Rome's urban fare ring is **€8**. ADR says it stops at Rome stations **such as Tiburtina and Ostiense**, with trains **every 15 minutes on working days and every 30 minutes on weekends and holidays**.

Neither Trenitalia nor ADR publishes a journey time for the FL1 on the pages we read, so we don't give one here. Check the time for your exact station on the Trenitalia journey planner. If your hotel is near one of its stations, the FL1 can save both money and a change at Termini.

## The ticket rule that costs people €50

Paper regional tickets (FL1) **must be validated before you board**: at Fiumicino airport station that means at the turnstiles. Once validated, a paper single is good for 90 minutes. Digital tickets bought on the Trenitalia app or website are validated automatically.

The penalties come from Trenitalia's regional fare rules for Lazio:

- Travelling with a ticket you didn't validate costs **€100**, cut to **€50** if you pay within five days.
- If you tell the conductor as you board, they validate it for **€5**.
- An €8 FL1 ticket is not valid on the Leonardo Express. Use one there without telling staff and you pay an **€8 surcharge plus the €6 difference**.

## Taxis: €55 a car, fixed, to the historic centre

Rome's mobility agency, Roma Servizi per la Mobilità, sets a **fixed fare of €55 per car** from Fiumicino to anywhere **inside the Aurelian Walls**, the old city walls that enclose most of the historic centre. The fare includes all supplements, and the agency puts the trip at **about 40 to 50 minutes**. ADR's taxi page gives the same €55. From Fiumicino the agency also lists fixed fares of **€60 to Tiburtina station** and **€50 to Ostiense station**.

Official taxis are **white, with a "TAXI" sign on the roof and a licence number on the doors**. The ranks are on the **Arrivals level of Terminals 1 and 3**. ADR says taxis operate 24 hours a day.

The maths changes with the size of your group. For one person the taxi costs nearly four times the train. Four people heading to Termini pay €40 together on the Leonardo group fare, against €55 for the taxi. The taxi takes you to your door and the train leaves you at Termini, so for a hotel far from a metro stop, or with a lot of luggage, the taxi is usually worth the difference.

Arriving at **Ciampino**, the smaller airport, instead? The fixed fare from Ciampino to inside the Aurelian Walls is **€40 per car**, about 30 minutes, according to the same agency.

## Buses: the cheapest seats, if time is not tight

Three companies run coaches from Fiumicino to central Rome. Their stands are outside the terminal. ADR's bus page puts SIT at stand 16 and Terravision at stand 18, and the operators' own pages agree.

- **SIT Bus Shuttle**: **€7** one way bought online (€13 return), with **€2 extra** if you buy at the stop. It stops at Circonvallazione Aurelia 19, Via Crescenzio 19 near the Vatican, and Termini (Via Marsala 5). Airport departures run from **07:15 to 01:15**, which makes it useful for late flights. SIT calls its travel times "indicative". The Tiqets listing for the same bus, which we read on 29 October 2026, gives about 50 minutes.
- **Terravision**: adult fares **from €4** one way online, with buses **every 20 minutes** to Termini. Its page gives the journey as anything from 40 to 50 minutes.
- **Cotral**, the regional bus company: **€5**, or **€7** if bought on board. Its ticket page describes these as night runs from Termini and Tiburtina.

The catch with any bus is traffic: the trip is only as fast as the roads into Rome that day. If you have a train to catch or a timed entry booked, take the Leonardo Express.

## Pre-booked private transfers

A pre-booked driver meets you at arrivals with your name, tracks your flight and drives you to the door. Welcome Pickups' Rome page, which we read on 8 October 2026, describes a **flat, pre-paid fee "equivalent to a taxi from the rank"**, flight monitoring and 24/7 support. The airport price only appears once you enter passengers and luggage, so compare it with the €55 taxi fare for your own group before you pay. A transfer is most worth it after a late or delayed flight, with small children, or when you would rather not queue at the rank.

## Which one to choose

- **On your own, or two people, staying near Termini or a metro stop:** Leonardo Express.
- **Staying near Tiburtina or Ostiense:** the FL1 at €8, but validate the ticket.
- **Three or four people with luggage, staying inside the walls:** a licensed taxi at €55 for the car.
- **On a tight budget with time to spare, or landing late:** SIT or Terravision.
- **A late arrival, children or lots of bags:** a pre-booked transfer, if its quote is close to the taxi fare.
